speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs how did the two brands of aluminium composite panel used as external cladding that were recently found to pose potential fire risk come to possess Class "0" certificates and how did the SCDF discover that they could pose fire risks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I need to know from the Non-Constituency Member of Parliament, he said there were two brands of aluminium composite panel – is he referring to the Bolliya and Bolli-Core FR?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Industry partners meaning building owners, qualified persons (QPs) and so on.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The building owner then informed the SCDF about the matter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And this is referring to the certification system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Another set of questions is: whether SCDF will be extending the retesting to all brands of cladding?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And if so, when will this be completed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Whether SCDF will be extending the retesting to all brands of cladding?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And if so, when will this be completed?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On whether the integrity of certification systems been compromised, I think that will be too quick a conclusion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Again, I need to be careful about what I say because the matter is under, not just SCDF investigations, but also Police investigations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SCDF has issued a public statement as to how it believes non-compliant panels came to be put up on the structures.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we go back to the public statement by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), there was one type of cladding which complied with the certification requirements, another that could not be used on the façade.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SCDF believes they had been mixed up in the warehouse.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it is not a question of integrity of the testing system.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But if you had asked me to speculate in August as to how this came about, I think it would have been difficult for me to have speculated that it is because there was a mixture in the warehouse.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One has got to be careful about jumping to conclusions, at this point, as to whether the entire certification system has been compromised.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The certification system relies on identifying international institutions of repute, which are recognised worldwide, and also institutions in Singapore, which can either rely on those certificates and make sure that the testing has been done, or test themselves.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I think we will obviously be investigating all possibilities, including whether there could be manufacturing defects, and differences between samples and actual material.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have answered the Non-Constituency Member of Parliament previously, sampling is the method worldwide.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The way of testing is to burn the material.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And by definition, if you want to do a 100% testing, there will be no material left.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As to how this will be reviewed in the context of public safety – in all the things that we do, I think that is front and centre.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Everything else has got to work around public safety, which is why, for example, let us take this issue of cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In contrast with what happened at Grenfell Tower, Cladding is one aspect.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How does it compromise public safety depends on a variety of factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, is the entire building clad with this material?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we say 5% of the building façade is clad with this material, obviously, the risk is very different from 100% cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of the buildings identified have less than 5%, less than 8%.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, that is one factor – how much of the building has been clad with such a cladding?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Second, what sort of fire sprinkler system is there?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member would know the contrast with Grenfell Tower again.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In Singapore, the requirements for, for example, the fire escape routes are very stringent and they have to be fire protected as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These are composite factors and then there are other aspects of safety like how much training do the staff have in commercial buildings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, SCDF, in respect of these buildings, has gone down to look at all these aspects together and worked with the management, while they are taking down the cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because even for buildings with 5% or 8% of cladding, we require them to take down, and at the same time, we are making sure that these other, what I call the human safety factors, are being practised.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Fire safety is absolutely important, which is why SCDF makes that assessment first, while the testing is going on, because testing takes some time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But they make an assessment as to whether the building is safe or not safe and announce it publicly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where there is no unrestricted public access to the buildings, SCDF requires the building owners to inform all their tenants of the nature of the cladding and the issues surrounding it, so that the tenants can make a considered assessment.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Even though we say it is safe, we believe it is safe, but we think the tenants ought to know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where there is unrestricted public access, we think that should be made public and it is up on the SCDF's website.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the approach that is taken, and regardless of whether it is 5%, 8%, 10% or 50% cladding, we require them to take it down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The other four are in the process of taking down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another building, a church, has been identified more recently.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We are in the process of talking to them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, all of them are in the process of being taken down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In respect of other brands of cladding, what is doable has been done, in the sense that we have contacted industry partners, we have required QPs to give us returns to explain and relook at their buildings, make second round of checks.
